ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Ronald Reagan — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints from him or his caregivers. [S]

Mr. Reagan is a 90-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer's disease (FAST stage 5) who returns for his subsequent annual wellness visit, three months after his six-month review after the right hip fracture repair. He answered the health risk assessment himself, with a caregiver reading each question aloud and confirming the answers he could not recall. He has had no falls, emergency visits, or hospital stays since he went home after the operation. He walks in the house and garden with a front-wheeled walker and standby supervision. His caregivers give his medicines from a weekly organizer and report no missed doses and no new over-the-counter medicines or supplements. The evening restlessness is mild and unchanged, and an unhurried evening routine still settles it. He says he feels well and enjoys his time outdoors. [S]

Follow-up: Yearly dementia review with MoCA, FAST stage, ADL and IADL scores, and the Zarit Burden Interview in about four months. Calcium and kidney function before the second zoledronic acid infusion in about six months. Next annual wellness visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent, with the patient taking part as he was able and his health care agent present. The health care agent named earlier this year and the POLST form completed in the spring were reviewed and remain unchanged. He said he wants to stay at home. The discussion covered what the later stages of Alzheimer's disease can bring, including trouble with eating and swallowing and more frequent infections, careful hand feeding as an alternative to tube feeding, the place of hospital transfer, and hospice when he becomes eligible. No decisions were changed today. The plan will be revisited at any change in stage or after a hospital stay. [S]
